reuters-dnr-2025.name: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2025: executive summary

real-fake-online.name: Worried about what is real and fake online
real-fake-online.passage: more than half of our respondents worldwide (58%) agree that they are worried about what is real and fake online when it comes to news

misinfo-sources.name: Influencers and national politicians seen as the biggest sources of false or misleading information
misinfo-sources.passage: online influencers and personalities are seen as the biggest threat worldwide (47%), along with national politicians (47%)

trust-in-news.name: Overall trust in the news
trust-in-news.passage: overall trust in the news (40%) has remained stable for the third year in a row, even if it is still four points lower overall than it was at the height of the Coronavirus pandemic

news-avoidance.name: Sometimes or often avoid the news
news-avoidance.passage: Across markets, four in ten (40%) say they sometimes or often avoid the news, up from 29% in 2017 and the joint highest figure we’ve ever recorded (along with 2024).

news-overload.name: Selective avoiders who struggle with news overload
news-overload.passage: selective avoiders who struggle with news overload and look to protect themselves at certain times or for particular topics

local-news-future.name: Deepening concerns about the future of local news
local-news-future.passage: there are deepening concerns about the future of local news. In the United States and much of Europe, local and regional newspapers have struggled to adapt to the shift to digital

content-moderation.name: Platforms removing too little (or too much) harmful content
content-moderation.passage: Across our entire sample, people were almost twice as likely to say that platforms were removing too little rather than too much (32%/18%).

ai-less-trustworthy.name: AI expected to make news less accurate and less trustworthy
ai-less-trustworthy.passage: Across countries they expect that AI will make the news cheaper to make (+29 net difference) and more up-to-date (+16) but less transparent (-8), less accurate (-8), and less trustworthy (-18).

gallup-media-trust-2025.name: Gallup: trust in mass media (September 2025 poll)

trust-mass-media.name: Trust in newspapers, television and radio to report the news fully, accurately and fairly
trust-mass-media.passage: Americans’ confidence in the mass media has edged down to a new low, with just 28% expressing a “great deal” or “fair amount” of trust in newspapers, television and radio to report the news fully, accurately and fairly. This is down from 31% last year and 40% five years ago . Meanwhile, seven in 10 U.S. adults now say they have “not very much” confidence (36%) or “none at all” (34%).

pew-data-privacy-2023.name: Pew Research Center: How Americans View Data Privacy (2023)

government-data-use.name: Worried about how the government uses people’s data
government-data-use.passage: The share who say they are worried about government use of people’s data has increased from 64% in 2019 to 71% today.

little-control.name: Little to no control over what companies or the government do with their data
little-control.passage: Most believe they have little to no control over what companies or the government do with their data. While these shares have ticked down compared with 2019 , vast majorities feel this way about data collected by companies (73%) and the government (79%).

dont-understand-company-use.name: Understand little to nothing about what companies do with their data
dont-understand-company-use.passage: Some 67% say they understand little to nothing about what companies are doing with their personal data, up from 59%.

ai-data-use.name: Company use of AI will lead to personal information used in uncomfortable ways
ai-data-use.passage: its use by companies will lead to people’s personal information being used in ways they won’t be comfortable with (81%) or that weren’t originally intended (80%)

kids-online-privacy.name: Concerned about social media platforms knowing personal information about kids
kids-online-privacy.passage: Some 89% are very or somewhat concerned about social media platforms knowing personal information about kids.

fraudulent-charges.name: Fraudulent charges on a debit or credit card
fraudulent-charges.passage: Roughly one-quarter of Americans (26%) say someone has put fraudulent charges on their debit or credit card in the last 12 months.

accounts-taken-over.name: Email or social media accounts taken over without permission
accounts-taken-over.passage: And 11% have had their email or social media accounts taken over without permission, while 7% have had someone attempt to open a line of credit or apply for a loan in their name. All told, 34% have experienced at least one of these things in the past year.

pew-online-harassment-2021.name: Pew Research Center: The State of Online Harassment (2021)

online-harassment.name: Personally experienced online harassment
online-harassment.passage: 41% of U.S. adults have personally experienced online harassment, and 25% have experienced more severe harassment

harassment-a-problem.name: People being harassed or bullied online is a problem
harassment-a-problem.passage: Roughly nine-in-ten Americans say people being harassed or bullied online is a problem, including 55% who consider it a major problem.

pew-ai-2025.name: Pew Research Center: How Americans View AI and Its Impact on People and Society (2025)

cant-detect-ai.name: Not confident they can tell if something was made by AI or a person
cant-detect-ai.passage: most Americans (76%) say it’s extremely or very important to be able to tell if pictures, videos and text were made by AI or people. But 53% of Americans are not too or not at all confident they can detect if something is made by AI versus a person.

pew-social-media-2020.name: Pew Research Center: social media’s effect on the country (2020)

social-media-negative.name: Social media have a mostly negative effect on the way things are going in the country
social-media-negative.passage: About two-thirds of Americans (64%) say social media have a mostly negative effect on the way things are going in the country today, according to a Pew Research Center survey of U.S. adults conducted July 13-19, 2020.

itrc-breaches-2025.name: Identity Theft Resource Center 2025 Data Breach Report (as reported by GovTech; idtheftcenter.org blocked the fetch)

data-compromises.name: Data compromises in the U.S.
data-compromises.passage: Data compromise incidents hit a record of 3,322 in 2025, with 70 percent of related breach notices failing to explain how the breach happened, according to a new report from the Identity Theft Resource Center (ITRC).

freedom-forum-2025.name: Freedom Forum: Where America Stands on the First Amendment, 2025 key takeaways (copy at MTSU First Amendment Encyclopedia; freedomforum.org returned 403)

afraid-to-speak.name: Fearful of consequences for speaking freely
afraid-to-speak.passage: Among the 65% who say in the survey they are fearful, they most often cited the threat of a violent response and fear of creating tension with friends and family.

free-press-threatened.name: Free press seen as the most threatened of the five freedoms
free-press-threatened.passage: The survey also found Americans see a free press as the most threatened of the five freedoms under President Trump.

press-freedom-difficult.name: Global state of press freedom classified as a difficult situation
press-freedom-difficult.passage: the global state of press freedom is now classified as a “difficult situation” for the first time in the history of the Index

oecd-truth-quest.name: OECD Truth Quest Survey (2024), as reported by Swissinfo; oecd.org returned 403

identify-false-content.name: Ability to tell true from false content online
identify-false-content.passage: Across all countries, participants managed to correctly identify the statements as true or false in 60% of cases.

sdg-targets.name: UN SDG targets bearing on information

16.10.name: Ensure public access to information and protect fundamental freedoms
16.10.passage: Target 16.10 Ensure public access to information and protect fundamental freedoms, in accordance with national legislation and international agreements

16.10.1.name: Killing, kidnapping, disappearance, detention and torture of journalists and human rights advocates
16.10.1.passage: Target 16.10 - In 2024, the number of killings of human rights defenders, journalists and trade unionists remained alarmingly high, with at least 502 cases reported across 44 countries

9.c.name: Universal and affordable access to the Internet
9.c.passage: Target 9.c Significantly increase access to information and communications technology and strive to provide universal and affordable access to the Internet in least developed countries by 2020

4.4.1.name: Youth and adults with information and communications technology (ICT) skills
4.4.1.passage: 4.4.1 Proportion of youth and adults with information and communications technology (ICT) skills, by type of skill

5.b.name: Use of information and communications technology to empower women
5.b.passage: Target 5.b Enhance the use of enabling technology, in particular information and communications technology, to promote the empowerment of women

17.8.name: Technology bank and ICT capacity for least developed countries
17.8.passage: Target 17.8 Fully operationalize the technology bank and science, technology and innovation capacity-building mechanism for least developed countries by 2017

Q13.name: Information needed in daily life
Q13.passage: 13 How available to you is the information you need in your daily life?

understanding.name: Understanding (satisfiers include communication policies)
understanding.passage: Understanding critical conscience, receptiveness, curiosity, astonishment, discipline, intuition, rationality literature, teachers, method, educational policies, communication policies

censorship.name: Censorship as a violator of understanding, participation and freedom
censorship.passage: But also censorship, for satisfying the need for protection, but for preventing satisfying the needs of understanding, participation and freedom.

propaganda.name: Advertising and propaganda as pseudo-satisfiers
propaganda.passage: They derive from advertising or propaganda ('pseudo-satisfiers'). May satisfy a need for a time, but make it less likely to meet the need in the future.

211-impact-2025.name: United Way 211 Impact Snapshot 2025: information and referral

information-referral.name: Information and referrals to social services programs and resources
information-referral.passage: In 2025, 211 community resource specialists made 19 million referrals for locally available help, 1 million more than in 2024

census-language-2019.name: U.S. Census Bureau: languages spoken at home and English-speaking ability (2019 ACS)

limited-english.name: Speak English less than very well
limited-english.passage: Based on the 2019 data, 52% of people who spoke Chinese and 57% of those who spoke Vietnamese at home in the United States spoke English “less than very well,” compared to the other three common languages: Spanish 39%, Tagalog 30%, and Arabic 35%
